findings.title: Recurring cancel deletions never awaited
findings.body: In handleCancelBooking.ts the code iterates calendar credentials with `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)) })`. A `forEach` with an async callback is fire-and-forget; the outer function does not await the callbacks. Later the code does `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`, but at that point `apiDeletes` has not yet been populated by the still-pending callbacks. Consequence: for recurring cancellations with `allRemainingBookings`, calendar deletions are lost or race with the response, leaving stale events on external calendars and incorrect availability.

findings.title: Reschedule deletions fire-and-forget via async forEach
findings.body: In bookings.tsx `requestReschedule` does `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { if (...) { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); } else ... return deleteMeeting(...) })` with no await on the loop and no `Promise.all`. The returned promises from `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` are also not awaited or collected. Consequence: the handler sends the reschedule email and webhooks before old calendar/video events are deleted, failures become unhandled rejections, and old time slots may never be freed, causing double-bookings.

findings.title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletes unawaited
findings.body: In vital/lib/reschedule.ts the code does `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); return deleteMeeting(...) })` inside a `try` block. `forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the `try/catch` cannot catch asynchronous rejections and the function proceeds to send email and `return true` immediately. Consequence: deletion errors are silently lost as unhandled rejections and reschedule can report success while external calendar/video events remain.

Consequence: deletion errors are silently lost as unhandled rejections and reschedule can report success while external calendar/video events remain.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in sync API
findings.body: In CalendarManager.ts `getCalendarCredentials` is still a synchronous function but now does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` where `getCalendar` is async and returns `Promise<Calendar|null>`. The returned objects therefore contain `calendar: Promise` instead of `Calendar|null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other consumer of this exported function expecting a truthy calendar instance or calling calendar methods directly will get a Promise object (always truthy) and fail. The contract change is invisible in the sync signature and breaks callers and type expectations.
